status: Exploratory transfer experiment, written before executing this extension; not an externally preregistered study
question: Which file-identity distinctions survive privacy filtering when real file reads are instrumented during execution?
claim_to_test: Literal aliases and lexical path normalization can both lose distinctions relevant to object-based file authorization. Resolved-path aliases and opened-object receipts have different coverage.
policy: Read only the filesystem object named by the approved path. Symlinks and hard links to that same object are authorized. This is object-based authorization, not a directory-confinement policy.
strongest_alternative: A log may never have recorded the filesystem bindings needed for authorization. Such missing evidence must not be attributed to filtering. Different file contents may also retain a distinction despite path filtering.

baselines.literal: Per-execution consistent aliases of literal path strings
baselines.realpath: Path.resolve(strict=True) against the unchanged live filesystem before aliasing
baselines.literal_receipt: Literal path aliases plus aliases of approved and opened (device,inode) identifiers, captured with fstat
baselines.raw_receipt: Same additional identity fields without anonymization, isolating instrumentation from filtering

measurement: Compare complete captured LangSmith POST/PATCH bodies. Count exact opposite-outcome collisions separately for each family and content condition. Do not equate distinct records with correct decisions.
checker: For receipt conditions only, compare approved-object and opened-object fields in the exported records. No gold label, path-to-object map, or live filesystem access is available to this checker.
controls: Hidden-binding pair with identical arguments but a changed symlink target
Actual bytes and fstat identifiers from the descriptor used to read
No network transport; fail on any unexpected HTTP URL
No concurrent filesystem mutation or race claims
cheapest_pilot: One identifier instance of every family, both content conditions, all representations
inclusion_rule: Add a concise paper result only if this tests a meaningful boundary beyond email case normalization. Retain every family, control, and unfavorable result in the artifact. A raw-log collision is an instrumentation gap. If this only repeats the existing finding without clarifying a deployment choice, leave it outside the manuscript.
stop_rule: Do not expand model count or sample size to make a routine or ambiguous result look stronger. Stop after the planned three identifier instances and controls if the harness is valid.
